title: One Day Out From Early Access, Emberville Has Been Delayed To 2027
description: Originally set to enter early access on October 27, action-adventure RPG Emberville has been delayed by over two months to January 7, 2027. The last-minute delay gives the team time to make "essential improvements" before Emberville reaches its fans. The upcoming game mixes Stardew Valley-like farming and community building with action-adventure RPG combat. Trapped in a magical underground dungeon, the player must uncover the truth about their cursed prison while revitalizing the ruined town of Emberville. Emberville's demo was one of the most played during Steam Next Fest last week; however, player feedback from the demo has led to a last-minute delay. "Some of the improvements we want to make are systems changes that can't be done quickly," the Emberville team said, acknowledging feedback from Next Fest players. "Reworking bow combat, for example, would take more time than we had prior to our Early Access release even though the team is working around the clock. After carefully considering our options, we have decided to move the release date and include some essential improvements in the Early Access launch build." While the game is intended to grow and improve throughout its early access period, with the developer planning to add new content incrementally, the studio wants to reach a certain baseline before it launches. "Our team has a clear vision for how Emberville will develop throughout early access," the Steam post continues. "On January 7, our goal is to deliver an experience that shows what makes the game distinctive, establishes its core gameplay, and offers a compelling glimpse of how the game will grow throughout early access." While some players are disappointed by the eleventh-hour delay, others have said they're happy for the Emberville team to take as much time as it needs to get the game up to scratch. Some players have also speculated that Emberville is just the latest game to move its release date in order to avoid losing players to the looming…

title: Ghost Of Yotei Was A Hit, But Its Developer Is Reportedly Cutting Jobs
description: Sony-owned studio Sucker Punch Productions is losing 24 employees in another round of layoffs in the games industry. The studio is behind Ghost of Tsushima and Ghost of Yotei, two first-party PlayStation titles that have been critical and commercial hits. An Aftermath report claims 24 Sucker Punch staff have lost their jobs. The studio is estimated to have between 190 and 230 staff, depending on the source, meaning Sucker Punch has lost at least 10% of its employees. "After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions," an email from studio leadership quoted by Aftermath read. "Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result." "We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can," the email continued, adding: "Next week we will go into more details about the future." For the past decade, Sucker Punch has worked on its two open-world samurai adventure games, both standout successes in Sony's first-party slate. As of 2022, Ghost of Tsushima had sold over 8 million lifetime copies, while Ghost of Yotei was reported to be Sony's best-selling title on the PS5 as of June 2026. The studio's latest release was the critically acclaimed Echoes of Sekigahara expansion for Ghost of Yotei, which brought back the first game's protagonist, Jin Sakai. Prior to Ghost of Tsushima, Sucker Punch developed the Sly Cooper and Infamous series. This isn't the first time the studio has undergone layoffs after a commercially successful release; an unspecified number of layoffs occurred in 2014 following the launch of Infamous Second Son, the same month the expansion First Light was released.

title: This Book Release Is Basically GTA 6 Launch For Thirsty Women, And Larian Knows It
description: You might have noticed that Baldur's Gate 3 has an extraordinarily large female audience, and for years, I've had my own theory as to why this is. Much like Dragon Age ( rest in peace, my sweet angel ), Baldur's Gate 3 features high stakes, fantasy-filled adventure, swords and sorcery, and charming characters that you can smooch. Essentially, it's a Romantasy--a term given to the plethora of women-oriented novels that feature all of the above. Regardless of if you love or hate the term, Romantasy has exploded in popularity over the past decade, and part of that is thanks to writer Sarah J. Maas and her A Court of Thorns and Roses series. For over five years, that series has been on hold while Maas worked on other novels, but now, the sixth book in the series, A Court of Splintered Harmony, is finally here--or at least it will be later tonight. Anyways, it's basically GTA 6 release day for thirsty women, and Larian's latest post proves that team is well aware of it. Earlier today, Larian took to Instagram to share a post referencing the series ahead of A Court of Splintered Harmony's release. In it, the studio shows off a few of the saga's most notable characters in Baldur's Gate 3's character creator while ACOTAR-related audio plays over top. But while Larian celebrating ACOTAR was already enough to made me giddy, the best thing about this post is that it proves that someone at Larian knows ball. Each clip perfectly pokes fun at a character's most iconic (or notorious) moment, or references an inside joke from the ACOTAR community. This includes Feyre's watery bowels, the invisible fleck of dust Rhysand is constantly picking at, and the fact that Feyre's garden-loving sister Elain probably could have helped her family and grown a few crops while they were, you know, starving to death in a small cottage. And the Withers-Suriel comparison? Masterful. Suffice to say that as both an avid reader and gamer, Larian's post delighted me. And as someone who has been yelling…

title: Here’s Another Mass Effect 5 Leak To Break Your Heart
description: If last week's mysterious Mass Effect: Universe trailer leak wasn't painful enough for you in the wake of BioWare's sudden closure, we've gotten yet another taste of The Game That Could Have Been, this time courtesy of award-winning video game composer Austin Wintory. Known for his beautiful and haunting soundtracks for games like Flow, Journey, ABZÛ, Aliens: Fireteam Elite, Sword of The Sea, John Wick Hex, and Hades II, Wintory was also evidently working on the Mass Effect: Universe soundtrack. From the sounds of things, EA and the now-defunct BioWare were considering having Wintory produce the game's OST. And thanks to Wintory, we at least know what the game might have sounded like. "Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project," Wintory wrote in a post on Bluesky. "For the last couple years I'd been in discussion with BioWare & EA to take on the project, and as part of that, I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next. May as well share it!" Wintory shared the music alongside an image that reads, "Mass Effect: Universe, the music that might have been." "So here you go," Wintory added in a follow-up post linking to a YouTube upload of the test-run tracks. "Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilege." The video features 20 minutes of Wintory's experimental score, featuring seven unique tracks and one remix. Text displayed within the video itself also reveals more about the nature of Wintory's talks with EA and BioWare, along with his inspiration for the soundtrack. "In 2007, when the credits rolled on my first playthrough of Mass Effect, I remember calling a friend and saying, 'I can't believe I already know this will be among my favorite all-time games.' Usually, it takes the passage of time before we can be so sure something truly belongs to the ages, but in this case, the confidence was instantaneous," Wintory wrote. "This trilogy is my…

title: WoW: Forever Just Got Another Major Racial Ability Shakeup Before Launch
description: World of Warcraft: Forever's release is just around the corner, but developer Blizzard is making one final pass at the game's racial abilities before launch in response to beta feedback. In a forum post, WoW community manager Kaivax posted a list of significant changes to many of each race's unique abilities that players expressed concerns about during Forever's beta. Those changes include tweaks to tauren, humans, orcs, dwarves, and Skyborne elves. "In taking a final pass on these, we've prioritized racial identity, which means that some races will naturally be slightly more effective than others at certain combat roles," Blizzard said. "In some places where we had replaced role or class-focused racials with generic ones, we're rolling those changes back." The exception to that mindset is weapon-specialization abilities, Blizzard said, which existed for humans and orcs both in WoW Classic and early on in Forever's beta and made each race more effective with specific types of weapons. "While those have a strong fantasy component to them, it is not healthy in the long run for future raid and dungeon loot tables to be evaluated through the lens of 'required' weapon types," Blizzard said. "At the same time, we're doing a tuning pass on some of the remaining passive bonuses to help ensure that they aren't skewing outcomes in a way that limits player preferences." Humans, widely viewed by the community as one of the most "optimal" races to pick thanks to their powerful passive abilities, have lost some of their power in combat. Ruthless now only grants 1% critical strike chance instead of 2%. In exchange, their Human Spirit passive has been buffed from 5% to 10%. Tauren have seen some significant changes, with massive buffs to their unique Plainsrunning ability but a loss to some of their combat effectiveness. Plainsrunning will now grant 2% movement speed per stack up to a max of 60% increased movement speed, at the price of no longer increasing mounted movement speed…

title: Diablo 4’s War Plans Are Getting A Huge Upgrade In Season 16
description: Diablo 4's War Plans system is getting a major upgrade in Season 16, giving players even more control over their endgame activities and rewards. Developer Blizzard introduced War Plans earlier this year as part of the game's second (and last) expansion, Lord of Hatred. It's an endgame system where players can essentially create a playlist of endgame activities, along the way ranking up those activities via a skill tree to make them even more rewarding. It was a welcome addition, but unfortunately only gave players minimal control over what activities would appear as part of their plans. Players could also only reroll their War Plans a limited number of times, meaning if you didn't like a particular activity, oftentimes you were stuck having to do it. All of that looks to be changing in Season 16 with the addition of a new meta-progression system called War Plans Tactics. By completing War Plan activities, players will be able to invest points into the tactics tree to make it so certain activities are more likely to appear and specific types of rewards will drop. How players reroll their War Plans is also changing, with a new currency called Marks of Wisdom that will cap at 20 and should let players reroll their plans more often. As detailed by Blizzard in a blog post ahead of the season arriving on the Diablo 4 public test realm October 27, players will be able to assign up to three points into each endgame activity and up to three points into different types of rewards. "Earn points from completing War Plans activities, then invest these points into nodes to increase the chance of preferred activities or rewards appearing," Blizzard said. "This allows you to tailor your War Plans more closely with both your goals and playstyle." A look at Diablo 4 Season 16's War Plans Tactics skill tree. Putting at least one point into Helltides or Nightmare dungeons also grants the choice of increased chances for Greater Helltides and Escalation Nightmare dungeons, respectively.…

title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Players Discover A Secret Gun Printer In Multiplayer
description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 players have discovered an Easter egg on one of the multiplayer maps, which is tied to the 3D printer feature found in the DMZ extraction mode. This secret printer lets players grab different gun builds mid-match, and these weapons are fully customized with attachments. As previously discovered by Muggs1213 on Reddit, Modern Warfare 4's Cachette multiplayer map contains one of DMZ's 3D printers. In DMZ, this printer is used to craft essential gear and upgrades specific to the extraction mode, but in multiplayer this device offers random weapon blueprints. Cachette's 3D printer is easily overlooked, especially when you're hot in the action, but it's found upstairs in the map's Armory point-of-interest. There is a weapon inside the 3D printer at the start of each match, and anyone can break the printer case open and retrieve the item inside. So far, players have discovered random weapon builds for guns, such as the Sang 9MM pistol, the PPSH-41 submachine gun, Cronen Squall assault rifle, and the Mosin Nagant marksman rifle. These guns being offered are generally fully kitted five-attachment weapon builds. This printer might only offer random weapon builds, but this is still a fun nod to Modern Warfare 4's DMZ, and it can be helpful to new players who might not have many weapons or attachments unlocked. Modern Warfare 4 launched on October 23, and the game's first DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack, with proceeds going to Activision's charity that helps military veterans find new jobs after they leave the service. If you're just getting started with this new Call of Duty, you may also want to check out our rundown of the best MW4 multiplayer loadouts.

title: Total War: Warhammer 3 And DLC Are Cheaper Than Ever, And The Chaos Gods Approve
description: War. War never changes. But what does change is the price of some of the best strategy games. Total War: Warhammer 3 is a total blast, offering brilliant strategy set in the ever-excellent fantasy Warhammer universe, and you can grab the game and its DLC for less than ever right now, including the newly launched Lords of the End Times expansion. As someone who doesn’t play the Warhammer (or Warhammer 40,000) tabletop games, the video games based on the franchise are some of my favorites. Vermintide? Absolute banger. Mechanicus remains one of my most-played strategy experiences (we don’t talk about the sequel here). Total War: Warhammer 3, however, feels the most impressive, both in the sheer scale of its battles and in how fun it is to control your own army. You start each playthrough by picking one of the Lords, leading your race of choice to victory—and whatever that means differs between the various characters. With rifts opening across the Mortal World and leading to the Realm of Chaos, the goal is to establish your empire as you seek Ursun, who is trapped in the realm. Whatever happens next is entirely dependent on your chosen Lord. Between intense battles, you’ll be required to do the more… mundane stuff, so to speak. That doesn’t make it dull, though, as upgrading your army and planning for future battles are just as important as the fighting itself. However, when you eventually end up at war with another kingdom, it’s all about leading your army, making hard choices, and thinking tactically to ensure you win. No one likes losing, after all. Total War: Warhammer 3 is an absolute blast, and it’s even better when you get it cheaper. In fact, you can get a Steam key for the game for just $7.79 / £6.49 at Fanatical. Who knew that starting a war could be so cheap? And if you enjoy the base game, several DLCs are also discounted at Fanatical right now, including: Forge of the Chaos Dwarfs - 64% off Ogre Kingdoms - 55% off Champions of Chaos - 55% off Lords of the…

title: Why There Won’t Be A Helldivers 3 Anytime Soon, If Ever
description: Helldivers 2 has been a huge hit for developer Arrowhead and publisher Sony, but don't expect a third game in the series anytime soon. Arrowhead's chief creative officer, Johan Pilestedt, told Rock Paper Shotgun that a sequel would reset "everything" and force the player to "start over." He doesn't want to ask the community to do that, so Arrowhead will instead keep the momentum going with the existing game by offering new content. "Some studios can treat players like a short-term cash grab," Pilestedt said. "We see players as the actual engine of the game: they're the ones bringing in friends, making memes, and keeping the game alive. When you have an active community doing that, you don’t need a sequel." He went on to say that the video game industry today is "panicking" because "the old live-service tricks don't work anymore," and that would also apply to a hypothetical Helldivers 3. If Arrowhead were to make a sequel, it would need to be highly differentiated, he said. "The biggest competitor to a Helldivers 3 would be Helldivers 2. It only makes sense to make a distinct sequel if it’s so different that both games can exist side by side. For now, making Helldivers 2 better every day makes way more sense than throwing away its momentum," he said. Pilestedt added that 95% of the studio is working on Helldivers 2 right now, with only a small team assigned to work on whatever the team is making next. While there won't be a third Helldivers game anytime soon, if ever, a Helldivers movie is now in the works. The very large man Alan Ritchson is replacing the very large Aqua(man) Jason Momoa as the film's lead.

title: The Scariest Game Of The Year Is This Demo For A Game That Isn’t Coming Out
description: It was a devastating gut punch when I sat down earlier this year to write about Paranormal Activity: Threshold only to discover it had been canceled and I'd missed the news. I'm not a huge fan of the movie series, though I do like the first few entries. Instead, my enthusiasm came from who was making the game: DarkStone Digital, creator of The Mortuary Assistant. I find The Mortuary Assistant to be among the scariest games ever made, and I credit much of its effectiveness to its impeccable sound design, something the found-footage series relies on, too. DarkStone Digital felt like a perfect fit for a Paranormal Activity game, and I couldn't wait to play it myself. But when Paramount refused to give DarkStone more time to polish the game, the developers, understandably, backed out. I've mourned it ever since, but this past weekend, I got to enjoy a portion of the canceled project, and now so can you. Out now on Steam as a free demo, Playable Archive is DarkStone's unfinished work, released as a "form of personal healing," studio owner Brian Clarke said in a press release. While Clarke never mentions Paranormal Activity by name, it's clear that Playable Archive is what's left of the now-canceled project. "After working for so long on something I cared so much about, it felt wrong to leave it sitting on the shelf like some cursed item," Clarke explained. "Although the full-scale game this demo was built for will never see the light of day and many pieces of it had to be left on the cutting room floor, I feel like it’s important to honor what was built." The 30- to 45-minute demo consists of first-person camcorder gameplay alongside a police investigation that occurs after all hell broke loose in a residence. By playing back tapes and solving occult puzzles, the investigator starts to piece together what went wrong. As a horror-obsessed person, I came away with two prevailing thoughts after finishing the demo: First, I was genuinely shaken by it, adding Playable…
